topic: Invest a sum all at once, or spread it out? In a study of global shares, all at once came out ahead about two thirds of the time

assumptions.notes: The lesson's 2023 fund manager study (Cost averaging: invest now or temporarily hold your cash?): global shares, 1976 to 2022, plus checks in the US, UK, Canada, Europe and Australia; investing at once beat spreading over 3 months about two thirds of the time over rolling one year periods, because shares and bonds beat cash most of the time. Bars to scale: 67 and 33. 'Dollar cost averaging' is not used. Numbers: three months, a year, two thirds.

caption.instagram:
Invest it all at once, or spread it out?

All at once, or in equal parts over three months. A study of global shares compared the results a year later: all at once came out ahead about two thirds of the time, and spreading in the rest.

Investments usually beat cash, so money waiting usually missed growth. Spreading puts less on a single day.

Past data, mostly developed markets: a tendency, not a promise.

Part 3: what if the inheritance is shares or a home?

→ Know someone with money to invest? Send them this.

Part of the Money, Compounding series: short reels on fine tuning a plan you already have.

Source: a 2023 study by a large fund manager, global markets 1976 to 2022, investing at once against spreading over three months. Not financial advice.
